_doc: Named calibration settings per voice, for the audition page. A key is a voice slug — the same string `make_audition.py` names its output directory, the set picker shows and a render's address carries — so `tools/voicematch/bank.py` is what says which keys are legal, and `test_calibration.py` fails on one that matches no voice. Each entry lists settings in the order they should appear on the page, after the unmodified build and before anything `--variant` adds on the command line. Read only when a run passes `--calibrations`: every setting is one more render of every take, and the override layer needs a -DBUILD_TUNING=ON library, so a page opened to hear one voice should not pay for it.
_overrides: The value of SONARE_TUNING_OVERRIDES, passed to the library untouched — the library is the only thing that can say whether a key exists. Keys are scoped: an engine constant is `<file stem>.<name>` (`brass_voice.kLipCouple`), a patch field is `<patch>.<path>` (`trumpet.brass.brassiness`), and a drum note's patch is `d038.percussion.wire_buzz`. A bare constant name resolves when it is unique across the tree and not otherwise — four voices declare `kBreathBase`. `autofit.py --out result.json` writes a paste-ready string, which is where most of these come from.
_note: What the setting is for, in one line, shown on the page under the version button. It is the only place a candidate says why it is a candidate: the override string says what moved and never says what it was trying to fix, and a page is read weeks after it was built.
_name: The source key: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`. It is the button label, the file stem and the last segment of the address, so what is on the button, what is in the URL and what is in a listening note are one string. `model` is taken by the unmodified build.
_open: A setting listed here is a candidate that has NOT been written back to the source. That is what the file is for: an override string kept only in a render directory under the scratch root is lost with the directory, and one harpsichord round's candidates were lost exactly that way. Recording is not adoption — a setting stays here until it is either written back (and deleted from here in the same change) or judged and deleted.

variants.name: softer-plectrum
variants.note: the reference is 5 dB down at h7 and up at h3

variants.name: more-rebased
variants.note: six mechanisms against the three dimensions still outside the reference spread: aftersound, stereo, vel_range

variants.name: more-as-heard
variants.note: the same six as first heard, on the decay of the time — its decay_slow_s 20.0 now undoes the committed 26.0, so more-rebased is the live question

variants.name: tank-3.6
variants.note: the organ's longer GS tank, on a voice that did not ask for it — the tank is host-wide, so this is what the organ's fix costs every other program

variants.name: tank-3.6
variants.note: the reference carries a 2 s hall the model cannot reach on the power-on tank

variants.name: hall
variants.note: the longer tank with the organ's own send pulled back, so the extra decay does not also arrive louder

variants.name: no-16
variants.note: the 16' rank all but silent — the registration question the three gated dimensions cannot settle

variants.name: perc-quiet
variants.note: half the shipped level: whether the ping sits under the registration or on top of it

variants.name: perc-loud
variants.note: the ping well forward, which is how a jazz registration is usually drawn

variants.name: drive-least
variants.note: the smallest drive that is not off, level-matched - the knob steps straight to tanh(x)/tanh(1), so this is the question of whether ANY amplifier belongs here

variants.name: drive-mild
variants.note: 1.5 dB of crest off a held chord, level-matched so loudness does not decide the choice

variants.name: drive-hard
variants.note: 2.9 dB of crest off, level-matched; the far end of what a rock organ's amplifier plausibly does

variants.name: di-fitted
variants.note: what a fit against the direct reference returns, and why it is not adopted: it takes the voice from 26.63 to 3.42 dB RMS of that reference above 2 kHz and takes program 29's whole chain from 4.93 to 23.29 dB of the amplified one. No rig recovers it - a cabinet only darkens, and the chain would need 27 dB more at 8 kHz - so the two references are not reachable together
